title.raw: 卷八十三 晉書9: 少帝本紀三 Volume 83 Book of Later Jin 9: Emperor Shao 3

sentences.zh: 開運元年秋七月辛未朔，帝御崇元殿，大赦天下，改天福九年為開運元年。

translations.literal: On the first day of the seventh month of autumn in the first year of Kaiyun, xinwei, the Emperor took the throne at Chongyuan Hall, proclaimed a general amnesty throughout the realm, and changed the ninth year of Tianfu to the first year of Kaiyun.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the seventh month in autumn of Kaiyun 1, xinwei, the Emperor held court in Chongyuan Hall, granted a general amnesty, and renamed the ninth year of Tianfu as the first year of Kaiyun.

sentences.zh: 河北諸州，曾經契丹蹂踐處，與免今年秋稅。

translations.literal: In all prefectures of Hebei that had suffered Khitan ravaging and trampling, the autumn tax of this year was remitted.
translations.idiomatic: All prefectures in Hebei that had been ravaged by the Khitan were granted exemption from this year's autumn tax.

sentences.zh: 諸軍將士等第各賜優給。

translations.literal: Officers and soldiers of the various armies were each granted generous rewards according to rank.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers and officers in the various armies received graded bonuses according to merit.

sentences.zh: 諸州率借錢帛，赦書到日，畫時罷征，出一千貫已上者與免科徭，一萬貫已上者與授本州上佐雲。

translations.literal: As for the forced loans of money and silk cloth levied by the prefectures, on the day the amnesty edict arrived collection was to cease at once; those who had paid one thousand strings or more were to be exempted from labor corvée, and those who had paid ten thousand strings or more were to be appointed to senior associate posts in their home prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Forced loans of cash and silk levied by the prefectures were to stop the moment the amnesty arrived; contributors of a thousand strings or more were freed from labor corvée, and those of ten thousand strings or more were to receive senior associate appointments in their home prefecture.

sentences.zh: 是日宣赦未畢，會大雷雨，匆遽而罷。

translations.literal: That day, before the proclamation of the amnesty was finished, a great thunderstorm occurred, and it was hurriedly brought to a close.
translations.idiomatic: That day the amnesty proclamation had not yet finished when a violent thunderstorm broke out, and the ceremony was cut short in haste.

sentences.zh: 時都下震死者數百人，明德門內震落石龍之首，識者以為石乃國姓，蓋不祥之甚也。

translations.literal: At that time several hundred people in the capital were killed by the quake; inside the Gate of Virtuous Clarity the head of a stone dragon fell from the shock, and those who understood such things held that stone was the dynastic surname—surely a most inauspicious sign.
translations.idiomatic: Several hundred people in the capital were killed by the earthquake, and inside the Gate of Virtuous Clarity the head of a stone dragon was shaken loose; the learned took stone to be the dynastic surname of the house—a dire omen indeed.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，以定州節度使馬全節為鄴都留守，加兼侍中；

translations.literal: On guiyou, Ma Quanjie, military governor of Dingzhou, was made military commissioner of Yedu, with the additional title of Vice Grand Counselor;
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou, Ma Quanjie, military governor of Dingzhou, was appointed military commissioner of Yedu and concurrently Vice Grand Counselor;

sentences.zh: 以昭義節度使安審暉為邢州節度使，加檢校太師。

translations.literal: An Shenhui, military governor of Zhaoyi, was made military governor of Xingzhou, with the additional title of Grand Preceptor by special appointment.
translations.idiomatic: An Shenhui, military governor of Zhaoyi, was transferred to Xingzhou as military governor and given the honorary title of Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，前陜州節度使王周加檢校太尉，改定州節度使；

translations.literal: On yihai, Wang Zhou, former military governor of Shaanzhou, was given the additional title of Grand Marshal by special appointment and transferred to military governor of Dingzhou;
translations.idiomatic: On yihai, Wang Zhou, former military governor of Shaanzhou, was made honorary Grand Marshal and appointed military governor of Dingzhou;

sentences.zh: 鄴都留守張從恩改鄆州節度使。

translations.literal: Zhang Cong'en, military commissioner of Yedu, was transferred to military governor of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Cong'en, military commissioner of Yedu, became military governor of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 禮官奏：「天子三年喪畢，祫享於太廟，高祖聖文章武明德孝皇帝今年八月喪終畢，合以十月行大祫之禮，冬季祠祭，改薦為祫。」

translations.literal: The ritual officials memorialized: "When the Son of Heaven's three-year mourning is completed, he performs the he sacrifice in the Grand Temple. The mourning for the Sagely, Cultured, Martial, and Virtuously Bright Filial Emperor Gaozu will be completed this eighth month; it is fitting to perform the great he rite in the tenth month, and for the winter seasonal sacrifices to change the jian offering to he."
translations.idiomatic: The ritual officials reported: "When the Son of Heaven completes three years of mourning, he offers the he sacrifice in the Grand Temple. Mourning for Emperor Gaozu, the Sagely, Cultured, Martial, and Virtuously Bright Filial Emperor, ends this eighth month; the great he rite should be held in the tenth month, and the winter seasonal sacrifices should be changed from jian to he."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The request was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，虞部員外郎、知制誥陶穀改倉部郎中、知制誥，大理卿吳德謙改秘書監致仕。

translations.literal: On dingchou, Tao Gu, Vice Director of the Bureau of Parks and Forests and drafter of edicts, was transferred to Director of the Bureau of Granaries and continued as drafter of edicts; Wu Deqian, Director of the Court of Judicial Review, was transferred to Director of the Palace Library and retired.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou, Tao Gu moved from Vice Director of Parks and Forests with edict-drafting duties to Director of the Bureau of Granaries while retaining his drafting post; Wu Deqian, Director of the Court of Judicial Review, became Director of the Palace Library and retired.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，以左龍武統軍李從敏為潞州節度使，天策府都護軍、桂州節度使、知郎州軍事馬希杲加檢校太師。

translations.literal: On xinsi, Li Congmin, Commander of the Left Dragon Martial Army, was made military governor of Luzhou; Ma Xigao, Protector-General of the Heavenly Stratagem Office, military governor of Guizhou, and supervisor of military affairs in Langzhou, was given the additional title of Grand Preceptor by special appointment.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi, Li Congmin, commander of the Left Dragon Martial Army, was appointed military governor of Luzhou; Ma Xigao, Protector-General of the Heavenly Stratagem Office and military governor of Guizhou with charge of Langzhou, received the honorary title of Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 壬午，降金州為防禦州，降萊州為刺史州。

translations.literal: On renwu, Jinzhou was reduced to a defense prefecture, and Laizhou was reduced to a prefecture under a prefect.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu, Jinzhou was downgraded to a defense command and Laizhou to a standard prefecture.

sentences.zh: 戶部侍郎田敏改兵部侍郎；

translations.literal: Tian Min, Vice Minister of Revenue, was transferred to Vice Minister of War;
translations.idiomatic: Tian Min, Vice Minister of Revenue, became Vice Minister of War;

sentences.zh: 刑部侍郎李祥改尚書右丞；

translations.literal: Li Xiang, Vice Minister of Justice, was transferred to Right Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs;
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiang, Vice Minister of Justice, was made Right Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs;

sentences.zh: 以潁州團練使馮玉為戶部侍郎，充端明殿學士；

translations.literal: Feng Yu, regimental commissioner of Yingzhou, was made Vice Minister of Revenue and appointed Academician of the Duanming Hall;
translations.idiomatic: Feng Yu, regimental commissioner of Yingzhou, was appointed Vice Minister of Revenue and Academician of the Duanming Hall;

sentences.zh: 中書舍人趙上交改刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: Zhao Shangjiao, Attendant Drafting Secretary of the Secretariat, was transferred to Vice Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Shangjiao, Attendant Drafting Secretary of the Secretariat, became Vice Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 己丑，以樞密使、中書令桑維翰充宏文館大學士，太子太傅、譙國公劉句為守司空兼門下侍郎平章事、監修國史、判三司，宰臣李崧、和凝進封爵邑。

translations.literal: On jichou, Sang Weihan, Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and Grand Counselor of the Secretariat, was appointed Grand Academician of the Hongwen Institute; Liu Gou, Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent and Duke of Qiao, was made Acting Minister of Works with concurrent appointment as Vice Director of the Chancellery, Grand Councilor, Supervisor of the National History, and Controller of the Three Commissions; the chief ministers Li Song and He Ning were advanced in noble rank and fief.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou, Sang Weihan, Commissioner of Military Affairs and Grand Counselor, became Grand Academician of the Hongwen Institute; Liu Gou, Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent and Duke of Qiao, was named Acting Minister of Works with concurrent posts as Vice Director of the Chancellery, Grand Councilor, Supervisor of the National History, and Controller of the Three Commissions; chief ministers Li Song and He Ning received promotions in rank and fief.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，宣徽北院使劉繼勛改宣徽南院使，三司使董遇改宣徽北院使。

translations.literal: On gengyin, Liu Jixun, Commissioner of the North Court of the Palace Secretariat, was transferred to Commissioner of the South Court of the Palace Secretariat; Dong Yu, Commissioner of the Three Commissions, was transferred to Commissioner of the North Court of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin, Liu Jixun moved from the North to the South Court of the Palace Secretariat; Dong Yu, Commissioner of the Three Commissions, took over the North Court post.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，以前陜州節度使石赟為鄧州節度使。

translations.literal: On xinmao, Shi Yun, former military governor of Shaanzhou, was made military governor of Dengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao, Shi Yun, former military governor of Shaanzhou, was appointed military governor of Dengzhou.

sentences.zh: 同州節度使李承福卒，贈太傅。

translations.literal: Li Chengfu, military governor of Tongzhou, died and was posthumously given the title of Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chengfu, military governor of Tongzhou, died and was posthumously honored as Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 八月辛丑，命十五將以禦契丹，

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on xinchou, fifteen generals were appointed to resist the Khitan,
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on xinchou, fifteen generals were ordered to take the field against the Khitan,

sentences.zh: 〈（《東都事略·範質傳》：晉出帝命十五將出征。

translations.literal: (From the 《Outline History of the Eastern Capital》 · Biography of Fan Zhi: The Deposed Emperor of Jin ordered fifteen generals on campaign.
translations.idiomatic: (From the 《Outline History of the Eastern Capital》 · Biography of Fan Zhi: The Deposed Emperor of Jin ordered fifteen generals on campaign.

sentences.zh: 是夕，質宿直，出帝命諸學士分草制，質曰：「宮城已閉，慮泄機事。」

translations.literal: That evening Fan Zhi was on night duty at court; the Deposed Emperor ordered the various academicians each to draft an edict, but Fan Zhi said, "The palace gates are already closed—there is fear of leaking military secrets."
translations.idiomatic: That night Fan Zhi was on palace duty. The Deposed Emperor told the academicians to divide the drafting of the edicts among themselves, but Fan Zhi said, "The palace gates are shut—we must not risk leaking military secrets."

sentences.zh: 遂獨為之。）〉

translations.literal: Thereupon he alone drafted them.)〉
translations.idiomatic: He therefore drafted them all himself.)〉

sentences.zh: 北京留守劉知遠充北面行營都統，鎮州節度使杜威充北面行營都招討使，鄆州節度使張從恩充馬步軍都監，西京留守景延廣充馬步軍都排陣使，徐州節度使趙在禮充馬步軍都虞候，晉州節度使安叔千充馬步軍左廂排陣使，前兗州節度使安審信充馬軍右廂排陣使，河中節度使安審琦充馬步軍都指揮使，河陽節度使符彥卿充馬軍左廂都指揮使，滑州節度使皇甫遇充馬步軍右廂都指揮使，右神武統軍張彥澤充馬軍排陣使，滄州節度使王廷胤充馬軍左廂都指揮使，陜州節度使宋彥筠充步軍右廂都指揮使，前金州節度使田武充步軍左廂排陣使，左神武統軍潘環充步軍右廂排陣使。

translations.literal: Liu Zhiyuan, military commissioner of the Northern Capital, was made overall commander of the northern campaign headquarters; Du Wei, military governor of Zhenzhou, was made overall commander for suppression; Zhang Cong'en, military governor of Yanzhou, was made overall supervisor of horse and foot armies; Jing Yanguang, military commissioner of the Western Capital, was made overall array marshal of horse and foot armies; Zhao Zaili, military governor of Xuzhou, was made overall deputy commander of horse and foot armies; An Shuqian, military governor of Jinzhou, was made array marshal of the left wing of horse and foot armies; An Shenxin, former military governor of Yanzhou, was made array marshal of the right wing of the cavalry; An Shenqi, military governor of Hezhong, was made overall commander of horse and foot armies; Fu Yanqing, military governor of Heyang, was made overall commander of the left wing of cavalry; Huangfu Yu, military governor of Huazhou, was made overall commander of the right wing of horse and foot armies; Zhang Yanzhe, Commander of the Right Divine Martial Army, was made cavalry array marshal; Wang Tingyin, military governor of Cangzhou, was made overall commander of the left wing of cavalry; Song Yanyun, military governor of Shaanzhou, was made overall commander of the right wing of infantry; Tian Wu, former military governor of Jinzhou, was made array marshal of the left wing of infantry; Pan Huan, Commander of the Left Divine Martial Army, was made array marshal of the right wing of infantry.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhiyuan, military commissioner of the Northern Capital, became overall commander of the northern campaign; Du Wei of Zhenzhou, overall commander for suppression; Zhang Cong'en of Yanzhou, overall supervisor of horse and foot; Jing Yanguang, military commissioner of the Western Capital, overall array marshal; Zhao Zaili of Xuzhou, overall deputy commander; An Shuqian of Jinzhou, left-wing array marshal; former Yanzhou governor An Shenxin, right-wing cavalry array marshal; An Shenqi of Hezhong, overall commander of horse and foot; Fu Yanqing of Heyang, left-wing cavalry commander; Huangfu Yu of Huazhou, right-wing horse-and-foot commander; Zhang Yanzhe of the Right Divine Martial Army, cavalry array marshal; Wang Tingyin of Cangzhou, left-wing cavalry commander; Song Yanyun of Shaanzhou, right-wing infantry commander; former Jinzhou governor Tian Wu, left-wing infantry array marshal; and Pan Huan of the Left Divine Martial Army, right-wing infantry array marshal.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，閩王王延羲為其下連重遇、朱文進所害，眾推文進知留後事，稱天福年號，間道以聞。

translations.literal: On renyin, the King of Min Wang Yanxi was killed by his subordinates Lian Chongyu and Zhu Wenjin; the multitude pushed Zhu Wenjin to manage the affairs of military commissioner, adopted the Tianfu era name, and reported by a secret route.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin, King Yanxi of Min was murdered by his officers Lian Chongyu and Zhu Wenjin; the troops installed Zhu Wenjin as acting military commissioner, proclaimed the Tianfu era name, and sent word by a back channel.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，太子少傅盧文紀改太子太傅，太子少保李麟改太子太保，刑部尚書李懌改戶部尚書，給事中司徒詡改右散騎常侍，以府州刺史折從阮為安北都護，充振武節度使。

translations.literal: On jiachen, Lu Wenji, Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent, was transferred to Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent; Li Lin, Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, was transferred to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent; Li Yi, Minister of Justice, was transferred to Minister of Revenue; Situ Xu, Attendant Censor, was transferred to Right Regular Attendant of the Cavalry; She Congruan, prefect of Fu Prefecture, was made Protector-General Pacifying the North and appointed military governor of Zhenwu.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen, Lu Wenji rose from Junior to Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent; Li Lin from Junior to Grand Guardian; Li Yi moved from Justice to Revenue; Situ Xu from Attendant Censor to Right Regular Attendant of the Cavalry; and She Congruan, prefect of Fu, was named Protector-General Pacifying the North and military governor of Zhenwu.

sentences.zh: 是夜，熒惑入南斗。

translations.literal: That night Mars entered the Southern Dipper.
translations.idiomatic: That night Mars entered the mansion of the Southern Dipper.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，詔復置明經、童子二科。

translations.literal: On yisi, an edict restored the two examination categories of Classicist and Youth.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi, an edict reinstated the Classicist and Youth examination tracks.

sentences.zh: 己酉，以鄧州節度使王令溫為延州節度使。

translations.literal: On jiyou, Wang Lingwen, military governor of Dengzhou, was made military governor of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou, Wang Lingwen, military governor of Dengzhou, was transferred to Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，以威武軍兵馬留後、權知閩國事朱文進為檢校太傅、福州威武軍節度使，知閩國事。

translations.literal: On guichou, Zhu Wenjin, military regent of the Weiwu Army and acting supervisor of the affairs of Min, was given the additional title of Grand Preceptor by special appointment and made military governor of the Weiwu Army at Fuzhou, with charge of the affairs of Min.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou, Zhu Wenjin, regent of the Weiwu Army and acting ruler of Min, received the honorary title of Grand Preceptor and was confirmed as military governor of the Weiwu Army at Fuzhou with authority over Min.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，升澶州為節鎮，以鎮寧為軍額，割濮州為屬郡。

translations.literal: On guihai, Chanzhou was elevated to a military commission, with Zhenning as the army designation, and Bozhou was carved out as its subordinate prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai, Chanzhou was raised to a full military commission under the army name Zhenning, with Bozhou detached to serve as its subordinate prefecture.

sentences.zh: 甲子，以延州節度使史威為澶州節度使。

translations.literal: On jiazi, Shi Wei, military governor of Yanzhou, was made military governor of Chanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi, Shi Wei, military governor of Yanzhou, was appointed military governor of Chanzhou.

sentences.zh: 九月庚午朔，日有蝕之。

translations.literal: On the first day of the ninth month, gengwu, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the ninth month, gengwu, the sun was eclipsed.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，以戶部侍郎韋勛為太子賓客，以前棣州刺史段希堯為戶部侍郎，以光祿卿張仁願為大理卿。

translations.literal: On yiyou, Wei Xun, Vice Minister of Revenue, was made Mentor of the Heir Apparent; Duan Xiyao, former prefect of Di Prefecture, was made Vice Minister of Revenue; Zhang Renyuan, Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, was made Director of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou, Wei Xun, Vice Minister of Revenue, became Mentor of the Heir Apparent; former Di prefect Duan Xiyao, Vice Minister of Revenue; and Zhang Renyuan, Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, Director of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 己丑，禮部侍郎符蒙卒。

translations.literal: On jichou, Fu Meng, Vice Minister of Rites, died.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou, Fu Meng, Vice Minister of Rites, died.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，太原奏，代州刺史白文珂破契丹於七里烽，斬首千餘級，生擒將校七十餘人。

translations.literal: On renchen, Taiyuan reported that Bai Wenke, prefect of Dai Prefecture, defeated the Khitan at Qilifeng, beheaded more than a thousand, and captured alive more than seventy officers.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen, Taiyuan reported that Bai Wenke, prefect of Dai, had routed the Khitan at Qilifeng, taking more than a thousand heads and seventy-odd officers alive.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，以前隴州防禦使翟光鄴為宣徽北院使。

translations.literal: On guisi, Zhai Guangye, former defense commissioner of Longzhou, was made Commissioner of the North Court of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi, Zhai Guangye, former defense commissioner of Longzhou, was appointed Commissioner of the North Court of the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 己亥，以滄州節度使王廷胤卒輟朝，贈中書令。

translations.literal: On jihai, because Wang Tingyin, military governor of Cangzhou, had died, court was suspended; he was posthumously given the title of Grand Counselor of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai, court mourning was observed for Wang Tingyin, military governor of Cangzhou, who was posthumously honored as Grand Counselor of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 冬十月壬寅，兩浙節度使、吳越國王錢宏佐加守太尉。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on renyin, Qian Hongzuo, military governor of the Two Zhes and King of Wuyue, was given the additional title of Acting Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter, on renyin, Qian Hongzuo, military governor of the Two Zhes and King of Wuyue, received the honorary title of Acting Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，以徐州節度使、北面行營馬步都虞候趙在禮為北面行營副都統，鄴都留守馬全節為北面行營副招討使。

translations.literal: On gengxu, Zhao Zaili, military governor of Xuzhou and overall deputy commander of horse and foot of the northern campaign headquarters, was made deputy overall commander of the northern campaign headquarters; Ma Quanjie, military commissioner of Yedu, was made deputy overall commander for suppression of the northern campaign headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu, Zhao Zaili of Xuzhou, deputy commander of the northern horse-and-foot forces, became deputy overall commander of the northern campaign, and Ma Quanjie, military commissioner of Yedu, deputy commander for suppression.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，以起居郎、知制誥賈緯為戶部郎中、知制誥。

translations.literal: On jiayin, Jia Wei, Recorder of the Heir Apparent and drafter of edicts, was made Director of the Bureau of Household Registers and continued as drafter of edicts.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin, Jia Wei, Recorder of the Heir Apparent with edict-drafting duties, became Director of the Bureau of Household Registers while retaining his drafting post.

sentences.zh: 戊午，詔曰：

translations.literal: On wuwu, an edict stated:
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu, an edict declared:

sentences.zh: 朕虔承顧命，獲嗣丕基。

translations.literal: We reverently received the dying charge and obtained succession to the great foundation.
translations.idiomatic: We have reverently received the late emperor's charge and succeeded to the great foundation of the realm.

sentences.zh: 常懼顛危，不克負荷，宵分日昃，罔敢怠寧，夕惕晨興，每懷祗畏。

translations.literal: We constantly fear overturn and ruin and are unable to bear the burden; from midnight to sunset we dare not slacken in repose, and rising in evening vigil and morning dread we ever harbor reverent awe.
translations.idiomatic: We constantly fear collapse and doubt our strength to bear the burden; from midnight until the sun sets we dare not rest, and waking each evening in vigil and each morning in dread, we live in reverent awe.

sentences.zh: 但以恩信未著，德教未敷，理道不明，咎征斯至。

translations.literal: Yet because grace and trust have not been made manifest, virtue and instruction have not been spread abroad, the Way of governance is not clear, and omens of blame have arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Yet grace and trust have not been established, virtue and instruction have not spread, the principles of rule remain unclear, and signs of blame have appeared.

sentences.zh: 向者，頻年災沴，稼穡不登，道堇相望，上天垂譴，涼德所招。

translations.literal: Recently, year after year there have been disasters and pestilence, the crops have not ripened, and the dead lie heaped along the roads; Heaven has lowered its reproof—what our meager virtue has drawn down.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years disasters and pestilence have recurred, harvests have failed, and corpses line the roads—Heaven's rebuke for our feeble virtue.

sentences.zh: 仍屬干戈尚興，邊陲多事。

translations.literal: Moreover arms are still raised and the frontiers are beset with many affairs.
translations.idiomatic: War still rages and the borders are troubled on every side.

sentences.zh: 倉廩不足，則輟人之糇食；

translations.literal: When the granaries are insufficient, we cut off the people's dry provisions;
translations.idiomatic: When the granaries run short, we seize the people's grain;

sentences.zh: 帑藏不足，則率人之資財；

translations.literal: when the treasury is insufficient, we levy the people's wealth;
translations.idiomatic: when the treasury fails, we levy the people's wealth;

sentences.zh: 兵士不足，則取人之丁中；

translations.literal: when soldiers are insufficient, we take men from the registered households;
translations.idiomatic: when troops are lacking, we conscript men from the registers;

sentences.zh: 戰騎不足，則假人之乘馬。

translations.literal: when war horses are insufficient, we borrow the people's riding horses.
translations.idiomatic: when war horses fall short, we press the people's mounts into service.

sentences.zh: 雖事不獲已，而理將若何！

translations.literal: Although the affairs could not be helped, what is to be said of the principle!
translations.idiomatic: Though necessity may excuse these acts, what can be said for the justice of them!

sentences.zh: 訪聞差去使臣，殊乖體認，不有敦於勉諭，而乃臨以威刑，自有所聞，益深愧悼。

translations.literal: On inquiry we have learned that the dispatched envoys have greatly departed from the intended understanding: instead of earnestly exhorting and instructing, they have confronted the people with harsh punishments; since we ourselves have heard of this, our shame and grief have deepened.
translations.idiomatic: We have learned that the envoys we dispatched utterly failed our intent: rather than urging and instructing the people, they met them with harsh punishments. Hearing this ourselves, we are all the more ashamed and grieved.

sentences.zh: 旋屬守臣叛命，敵騎入邊，致使甲兵不暇休息，軍旅有征戰之苦，人民有飛免之勞，疲瘵未蘇，科徭尚急，言念於茲，寢食何安！

translations.literal: Soon afterward border officials rebelled, enemy cavalry entered the frontier, causing armor and weapons to know no rest; the armies suffer the hardships of campaigning, the people the toil of fleeing like birds and hares; the weary and sick have not yet recovered, yet levies and corvée remain urgent—when we speak of this, how can we eat or sleep in peace!
translations.idiomatic: Soon border officials rebelled and enemy horsemen crossed the frontier, so that our armies know no rest, soldiers endure the hardships of campaign, and the people flee like startled game; the sick have not recovered, yet levies press on—at the thought of this, how can we eat or sleep in peace!

sentences.zh: 得不省過興懷，側身罪已，載深減損，思召和平？

translations.literal: Must we not examine our faults and rouse our hearts, turn inward and blame ourselves, deeply reduce expenditures, and seek to summon peace?
translations.idiomatic: Must we not examine our faults, turn inward in self-reproach, cut expenditures to the bone, and strive to restore peace?

sentences.zh: 所宜去無用之資，罷不急之務，棄華取實，惜費省功，一則符先帝慈儉之規，一則慕前王樸素之德。

translations.literal: What is fitting is to remove useless expenditures, abolish non-urgent tasks, discard ornament and take what is solid, cherish economy and save effort—on the one hand conforming to the late emperor's rule of kindness and frugality, on the other emulating the former kings' virtue of plain simplicity.
translations.idiomatic: We should cut useless spending, drop nonessential tasks, choose substance over display, and practice thrift—honoring the late emperor's kindness and frugality and emulating the plain virtue of kings of old.

sentences.zh: 向者，造作軍器，破用稍多，但取堅剛，不須華楚；

translations.literal: Recently, in manufacturing military weapons, expenditures have been rather heavy; what is needed is stout hardness, not ornate splendor;
translations.idiomatic: Recently the manufacture of arms has cost too much; what we need is strength and durability, not ornament;

sentences.zh: 今後作坊制器械，不得更用金銀裝飾。

translations.literal: henceforth workshops making equipment must no longer use gold and silver decoration.
translations.idiomatic: henceforth workshops must not trim weapons with gold or silver.

sentences.zh: 比於遊畋，素非所好，凡諸服禦，尤欲去奢，應天下府州不得以珍寶玩好及鷹犬為貢。

translations.literal: Compared with hunting, it has never been our preference; for all attire and equipage we especially wish to remove extravagance; throughout the realm no prefecture or district may present as tribute precious objects, curios, or hawks and dogs.
translations.idiomatic: We have never cared for the chase; for court dress and equipage we especially wish to banish luxury; no prefecture in the realm may present precious curios, playthings, hawks, or hunting dogs as tribute.

sentences.zh: 在昔聖帝明君，無非惡衣菲食，況於薄德，所合恭行，今後大官尚膳，減去多品，衣服帷帳，務去華飾，在禦寒溫而已。

translations.literal: In antiquity sage emperors and enlightened rulers all wore coarse clothes and ate plain food; how much more for one of slight virtue should this be respectfully practiced! Henceforth the Grand Steward and Director of Palace Provisions shall reduce the many dishes; for clothing, curtains, and canopies we shall strive to remove ornate decoration—sufficing only to guard against cold and heat.
translations.idiomatic: Sage rulers of old wore plain clothes and ate simple fare; how much more should we of meager virtue do the same! Henceforth the palace kitchens shall serve fewer dishes; clothing, curtains, and hangings shall shed ornament and serve only to keep off cold and heat.

sentences.zh: 峻宇雕墻，昔人所誡，玉杯象箸，前代攸非，今後凡有營繕之處，丹堊雕鏤，不得過度，宮闈之內，有非理費用，一切禁止。

translations.literal: Lofty halls and carved walls were what men of old warned against; jade cups and ivory chopsticks were what former ages condemned; henceforth wherever there is construction, cinnabar plaster and carved tracery must not be excessive, and within the palace quarters any unreasonable expenditure is altogether forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Lofty halls and carved walls were condemned by the ancients, jade cups and ivory chopsticks by former ages; henceforth all construction must avoid excessive plaster and carving, and every unreasonable expense within the palace is forbidden.

sentences.zh: 於戲！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 繼聖承祧，握樞臨極，昧於至道，若履春冰。

translations.literal: Succeeding the sage and receiving the ancestral temple, holding the pivot and facing the pole star, ignorant of the utmost Way, as if treading spring ice.
translations.idiomatic: Having inherited the sacred charge and taken the throne, we are ignorant of the highest Way and tread as upon spring ice.

sentences.zh: 屬以天災流行，國步多梗，因時致懼，引咎推誠，期於將來，庶幾有補。

translations.literal: Just now natural disasters are widespread and the state's steps are many times obstructed; in accord with the times we give rise to fear, draw blame upon ourselves and extend sincerity, hoping that in the future there may perhaps be some remedy.
translations.idiomatic: Disasters now ravage the land and the state staggers; in this hour we confess our faults and offer sincere repentance, hoping the future may yet be redeemed.

sentences.zh: 更賴王公、將相，貴戚、豪宗，各啟乃心，率由茲道，共臻富庶，以致康寧。

translations.literal: We further rely on princes and dukes, generals and ministers, noble kin and powerful clans each to open their hearts, follow this path, together attain wealth and plenty, and bring about peace and tranquility.
translations.idiomatic: We call upon princes, ministers, noble kin, and great houses to open their hearts, follow this course, and together bring prosperity and peace.

sentences.zh: 凡百臣僚，宜體朕意。

translations.literal: All officials should embody Our intent.
translations.idiomatic: Let every official take this edict to heart.

sentences.zh: 十一月壬申，詔曰：「蕃寇未平，邊陲多事，即日雖無侵軼，亦須廣設提防。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on renshen, an edict stated: "The barbarian invaders are not yet pacified and the frontiers have many affairs; although for the present there is no raiding, we must still broadly set up defenses.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on renshen, an edict declared: "The barbarian foe is not yet subdued and the borders remain troubled; though there is no raid today, defenses must be strengthened everywhere.

sentences.zh: 朕將親率虎貔，躬擐甲胄，候聞南牧，即便北征，不須先定日辰，別行告諭。

translations.literal: We shall personally lead the tiger guards, ourselves don armor, and when we hear that the enemy has driven south to pasture, at once march north; there is no need first to fix a date and separately issue notice.
translations.idiomatic: We shall personally lead our armies and don armor ourselves; when word comes that the enemy is driving south, we shall march north at once—no fixed date need be announced in advance.

sentences.zh: 所有供億，宜令三司預行計度，合隨從諸司職員，並宜常備行計」云。

translations.literal: All supplies and transport should be ordered planned in advance by the Three Commissions, and all officials of the various offices who are to accompany Us should constantly keep travel plans ready," it stated.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Commissions shall plan all supplies in advance, and every office whose staff will accompany Us shall keep travel arrangements in constant readiness," the edict concluded.

sentences.zh: 己卯，以陳州刺史梁漢璋充侍衛馬軍都指揮使。

translations.literal: On jimao, Liang Hanzhang, prefect of Chen Prefecture, was appointed overall commander of the palace guard cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao, Liang Hanzhang, prefect of Chen, was appointed overall commander of the palace guard cavalry.

sentences.zh: 壬午，以貝州節度使何建為澶州節度使兼北面行營馬軍右廂排陣使，以澶州節度使史威為貝州節度使。

translations.literal: On renwu, He Jian, military governor of Beizhou, was made military governor of Chanzhou with concurrent appointment as array marshal of the right wing of cavalry of the northern campaign headquarters; Shi Wei, military governor of Chanzhou, was made military governor of Beizhou.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu, He Jian of Beizhou became military governor of Chanzhou and right-wing cavalry array marshal of the northern campaign, while Shi Wei of Chanzhou was transferred to Beizhou.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，以前金州節度使田武為滄州節度使兼北面行營步軍右廂都指揮使，以前相州節度使郭謹為鄜州節度使。

translations.literal: On bingxu, Tian Wu, former military governor of Jinzhou, was made military governor of Cangzhou with concurrent appointment as overall commander of the right wing of infantry of the northern campaign headquarters; Guo Jin, former military governor of Xiangzhou, was made military governor of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu, former Jinzhou governor Tian Wu was appointed military governor of Cangzhou and overall commander of the northern campaign's right-wing infantry; former Xiangzhou governor Guo Jin became military governor of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 十二月己亥朔，幸臯門，射中白兔。

translations.literal: On the first day of the twelfth month, jihai, the Emperor visited Gao Gate and shot a white hare.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the twelfth month, jihai, the Emperor visited Gao Gate and shot a white hare.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，福州節度使朱文進加同平章事，封閩國王。

translations.literal: On guichou, Zhu Wenjin, military governor of Fuzhou, was given the additional title of Co-Grand Councilor and enfeoffed as King of Min.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou, Zhu Wenjin, military governor of Fuzhou, was made Co-Grand Councilor and enfeoffed as King of Min.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，青州楊光遠降。

translations.literal: On dingsi, Yang Guangyuan of Qingzhou surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi, Yang Guangyuan of Qingzhou surrendered.

sentences.zh: 光遠子承勛等斬觀察判官邱濤、牙將白延祚、楊贍、杜延壽等首級，送於招討使李守貞，乃縱火大噪，劫其父處於私第，以城納款，遣即墨縣令王德柔貢表待罪。

translations.literal: Guangyuan's sons Chengxun and the rest beheaded the observation commissioner Qiu Tao and the officers Bai Yanzuo, Yang Zhan, Du Yanshou, and others, and sent their heads to Li Shouzhen, the commander for suppression; then they set fires, raised a great uproar, seized their father and held him in a private house, surrendered the city, and dispatched Wang Derou, magistrate of Jimo, to present a memorial awaiting judgment.
translations.idiomatic: Guangyuan's sons Chengxun and the rest beheaded the observation commissioner Qiu Tao and the officers Bai Yanzuo, Yang Zhan, Du Yanshou, and others, and sent their heads to Li Shouzhen, the commander for suppression; then they set fires, raised a great uproar, seized their father and held him in a private house, surrendered the city, and dispatched Wang Derou, magistrate of Jimo, to present a memorial awaiting judgment.

sentences.zh: 楊光遠亦遣節度判官楊麟奉表請死。

translations.literal: Yang Guangyuan also sent his military commissioner Yang Lin to present a memorial requesting death.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Guangyuan also sent his aide Yang Lin with a memorial begging for execution.

sentences.zh: 詔釋之。

translations.literal: An edict pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: An edict granted him pardon.

sentences.zh: 閏月庚午，以楊承信為右羽林將軍，承祚為右驍騎衛將軍。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month, on gengwu, Yang Chengxin was made General of the Right Forest of Feathers Army, and Chengzuo was made General of the Right Valiant Cavalry Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month, on gengwu, Yang Chengxin was appointed General of the Right Forest of Feathers Army and Chengzuo General of the Right Valiant Cavalry Guard.

sentences.zh: 皆光遠之子，先詣闕請罪，故特授是官。

translations.literal: Both were sons of Guangyuan who had first come to court to plead guilt, and therefore were specially granted these offices.
translations.idiomatic: Both were Guangyuan's sons, who had come to court first to plead guilty; they were therefore specially granted these posts.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，李守貞奏，楊光遠卒。

translations.literal: On guiyou, Li Shouzhen memorialized that Yang Guangyuan had died.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou, Li Shouzhen reported that Yang Guangyuan had died.

sentences.zh: 初，光遠既上表送降，帝以光遠頃歲太原歸命，欲曲全之，議者曰：「豈有反狀滔天而赦之也！」

translations.literal: Initially, after Guangyuan had submitted his memorial offering surrender, the Emperor, because Guangyuan in recent years had submitted to the throne at Taiyuan, wished to spare him completely; but those in discussion said, "How can there be treason reaching to heaven and yet pardon him!"
translations.idiomatic: When Guangyuan had submitted his surrender memorial, the Emperor, remembering that he had once submitted at Taiyuan, wished to spare him; but critics said, "How can treason of such magnitude be pardoned!"

sentences.zh: 乃命守貞便宜處置。

translations.literal: Thereupon he ordered Shouzhen to dispose of the matter as circumstances required.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore ordered Shouzhen to act as he saw fit.

sentences.zh: 守貞遣人拉殺之，以病卒聞。

translations.literal: Shouzhen sent men to strangle him to death and reported it as death from illness.
translations.idiomatic: Shouzhen had him strangled and reported that he had died of illness.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，前登州刺史張萬迪削奪官爵處斬，青州節度判官楊麟配流威州，掌書記任邈配流原州，支使徐晏配流武州。

translations.literal: On yiyou, Zhang Wandi, former prefect of Deng Prefecture, was stripped of office and rank and executed; Yang Lin, military commissioner of Qingzhou, was banished to Weizhou; Ren Miao, chief secretary, was banished to Yuanzhou; Xu Yan, administrative aide, was banished to Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou, Zhang Wandi, former prefect of Deng, was stripped of rank and executed; Yang Lin, Qingzhou military commissioner, was banished to Weizhou; Ren Miao, chief secretary, to Yuanzhou; and Xu Yan, administrative aide, to Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 縱逢恩赦，不在放還之限，並以楊光遠叛故也。

translations.literal: Even if an amnesty should occur, they were not within the scope of release and return—all because of Yang Guangyuan's rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Even future amnesties would not restore them—all on account of Yang Guangyuan's rebellion.

sentences.zh: 工部尚書、權知貢舉竇貞固奏：「試進士諸科舉人入策，舊例夜試，以三條燭盡為限，天成二年改令晝試，今欲依舊夜試。」

translations.literal: Dou Zhengu, Minister of Works and acting supervisor of the examinations, memorialized: "Candidates for the jinshi and various categories who enter the policy examination—by old custom the test was at night, limited by the burning of three candles; in the second year of Tiancheng it was changed to daytime testing, and now we wish to follow the old custom of night testing."
translations.idiomatic: Dou Zhengu, Minister of Works and acting chief examiner, reported: "Jinshi and other candidates taking the policy examination formerly tested at night, with a limit of three candles; in Tiancheng 2 this was changed to daytime testing, and we now ask to restore the night examination."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The request was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved.

sentences.zh: 曲赦青州管內罪人，立功將士各賜優給，青州吏民為楊光遠詿誤者，一切不問。

translations.literal: A partial amnesty was granted to criminals within the jurisdiction of Qingzhou; meritorious officers and soldiers were each given generous rewards; officials and people of Qingzhou who had been misled by Yang Guangyuan were altogether not questioned.
translations.idiomatic: A partial amnesty was proclaimed for criminals in Qingzhou; meritorious soldiers received generous rewards; and officials and commoners misled by Yang Guangyuan were not prosecuted.

sentences.zh: 青州行營招討使、兗州節度使兼侍衛都虞候李守貞加同平章事，副招討使、河陽節度使符彥卿改許州節度使。

translations.literal: Li Shouzhen, commander for suppression of the Qingzhou field headquarters and military governor of Yanzhou with concurrent appointment as overall deputy commander of the palace guard, was given the additional title of Co-Grand Councilor; Fu Yanqing, deputy commander for suppression and military governor of Heyang, was transferred to military governor of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shouzhen, commander for suppression at the Qingzhou camp and military governor of Yanzhou with charge of the palace guard, was made Co-Grand Councilor; Fu Yanqing, deputy commander for suppression and military governor of Heyang, was transferred to Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，降青州為防禦使額，以萊州刺史楊承勛為汝州防禦使。

translations.literal: On bingxu, Qingzhou was reduced to a defense commission, and Yang Chengxun, prefect of Laizhou, was made defense commissioner of Ruzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu, Qingzhou was downgraded to a defense command, and Yang Chengxun, prefect of Laizhou, was appointed defense commissioner of Ruzhou.

sentences.zh: 己丑，以工部尚書竇貞固為禮部尚書，太常卿王延為工部尚書，左丞王松為太常卿，以前尚書右丞龍敏為尚書左丞。

translations.literal: On jichou, Dou Zhengu, Minister of Works, was made Minister of Rites; Wang Yan, Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, was made Minister of Works; Wang Song, Left Assistant Director, was made Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; Long Min, former Right Assistant Director, was made Left Assistant Director.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou, Dou Zhengu moved from Works to Rites; Wang Yan from Director of Sacrifices to Works; Wang Song from Left Assistant Director to Director of Sacrifices; and former Right Assistant Director Long Min to Left Assistant Director.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，以前安州防禦使李建崇為河陽兵馬留後，以宣徽使翟光鄴為青州防禦使，以內客省使李彥韜為宣徽北院使。

translations.literal: On guisi, Li Jianchong, former defense commissioner of Anzhou, was made military regent of Heyang; Zhai Guangye, Commissioner of the Palace Secretariat, was made defense commissioner of Qingzhou; Li Yantao, Commissioner of the Inner Clients Bureau, was made Commissioner of the North Court of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi, Li Jianchong, former defense commissioner of Anzhou, became military regent of Heyang; Zhai Guangye, Palace Secretariat commissioner, defense commissioner of Qingzhou; and Li Yantao, commissioner of the Inner Clients Bureau, commissioner of the North Court of the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 甲午，以給事中邊光範為左散騎常侍，以樞密直學士、吏部郎中李穀為給事中，依前充職。

translations.literal: On jiawu, Bian Guangfan, Attendant Censor, was made Left Regular Attendant of the Cavalry; Li Gu, Academician Direct of the Bureau of Military Affairs and Director of the Bureau of Personnel, was made Attendant Censor and continued in his former duties.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu, Bian Guangfan, Attendant Censor, became Left Regular Attendant of the Cavalry; Li Gu, Direct Academician of Military Affairs and Director of the Bureau of Personnel, was made Attendant Censor while retaining his former duties.

sentences.zh: 是月，契丹耶律德光與趙延壽領全軍入寇，圍恒州，分兵陷鼓城、槁城、元氏、高邑、昭慶、寧晉、蒲澤、欒城、柏鄉等縣，前鋒至邢州，河北諸州告急。

translations.literal: That month, Yelü Deguang of the Khitan and Zhao Yanshou led the full army in invasion, besieged Hengzhou, and with divided forces captured Gucheng, Gaocheng, Yuanshi, Gaoyi, Zhaoqing, Ningjin, Puze, Luancheng, Baixiang, and other counties; the vanguard reached Xingzhou, and all prefectures of Hebei reported urgent distress.
translations.idiomatic: That month Yelü Deguang of the Khitan and Zhao Yanshou invaded at the head of the full army, besieged Hengzhou, and sent detachments to seize Gucheng, Gaocheng, Yuanshi, Gaoyi, Zhaoqing, Ningjin, Puze, Luancheng, Baixiang, and other counties; the vanguard reached Xingzhou, and every prefecture in Hebei sent urgent alarms.

sentences.zh: 詔張從恩、馬全節、安審琦率師屯邢州，趙在禮屯鄴都。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Zhang Cong'en, Ma Quanjie, and An Shenqi to lead their armies and encamp at Xingzhou, and Zhao Zaili to encamp at Yedu.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Zhang Cong'en, Ma Quanjie, and An Shenqi to take the field and encamp at Xingzhou, while Zhao Zaili encamped at Yedu.

sentences.zh: 開運二年春正月戊戌朔，帝不受朝賀，不豫故也。

translations.literal: On the first day of the first month of spring in the second year of Kaiyun, wuxu, the Emperor did not receive court congratulations—because he was indisposed.
translations.idiomatic: On the new moon of the first month of spring in Kaiyun 2, wuxu, the Emperor declined the customary court felicitations, being still unwell.

sentences.zh: 己亥，張從恩部領兵士自邢州退至相州，人情震恐。

translations.literal: On jihai, Zhang Cong'en led his troops in retreat from Xingzhou to Xiangzhou, and popular sentiment was shaken with fear.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai, Zhang Cong'en withdrew his troops from Xingzhou to Xiangzhou, and panic spread among the people.

sentences.zh: 趙在禮還屯澶州，馬全節歸鄴都，遣右神武統軍張彥澤屯黎陽，詔西京留守景延廣將兵守胡梁渡。

translations.literal: Zhao Zaili returned to encamp at Chazhou; Ma Quanjie returned to Yedu; Right Commander of the Spirit Martial Army Zhang Yanzhe was sent to encamp at Liyang; and an edict ordered Western Capital regent Jing Yanguang to lead troops to hold Huliang Ford.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Zaili fell back to Chazhou; Ma Quanjie returned to Yedu; Zhang Yanzhe, Right Commander of the Spirit Martial Army, was posted at Liyang; and Jing Yanguang, regent of the Western Capital, was ordered to hold Huliang Ford.

sentences.zh: 契丹寇邢州。

translations.literal: The Khitan raided Xingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan attacked Xingzhou.

sentences.zh: 侍衛馬軍都指揮使梁漢璋改鄭州防禦使，典軍如故。

translations.literal: Liang Hanzhang, Commander of the Palace Cavalry, was transferred to defense commissioner of Zhengzhou, retaining command of the army as before.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Cavalry Commander Liang Hanzhang was made defense commissioner of Zhengzhou while keeping his military command.

sentences.zh: 以齊州防禦使劉在明為相州留後。

translations.literal: Liu Zaiming, defense commissioner of Qizhou, was made regent of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zaiming, defense commissioner of Qizhou, was appointed regent of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，以客省使孟承誨為內客省使。

translations.literal: On guimao, Meng Chenghui, Commissioner of the Clients Bureau, was made Commissioner of the Inner Clients Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao, Meng Chenghui, commissioner of the Clients Bureau, was promoted to commissioner of the Inner Clients Bureau.

sentences.zh: 滑州奏，今月二日至四日，相州路烽火不至。

translations.literal: Huazhou memorialized that from the second to the fourth of this month beacon fires on the Xiangzhou route had not arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Huazhou reported that from the second through the fourth of the month no beacon signals had come in from the Xiangzhou line.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，以前汝州防禦使宋光鄴為左驍衛大將軍。

translations.literal: On jiachen, Song Guangye, former defense commissioner of Ruzhou, was made Grand General of the Left Victorious Guard.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen, Song Guangye, former defense commissioner of Ruzhou, was appointed Grand General of the Left Victorious Guard.

sentences.zh: 詔青州行營將校，自副兵馬使以上，各賜功臣名號。

translations.literal: An edict granted meritorious service titles to the officers of the Qingzhou field headquarters, from deputy horse-and-arms commander upward.
translations.idiomatic: An edict awarded titles of meritorious service to the Qingzhou field officers, from deputy horse-and-arms commander on up.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，帝復常膳。

translations.literal: On yisi, the Emperor resumed his regular meals.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi, the Emperor returned to his normal diet.

sentences.zh: 以左武衛上將軍袁{山義}為客省使，上將軍如故。

translations.literal: Yuan [Yi], Senior General of the Left Martial Guard, was made Commissioner of the Clients Bureau, retaining his rank as senior general.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan [Yi], Senior General of the Left Martial Guard, was appointed commissioner of the Clients Bureau while keeping his rank as senior general.

sentences.zh: 詔滑州節度使皇甫遇率兵赴邢州，馬全節赴相州。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Huangfu Yu, military governor of Huazhou, to lead troops to Xingzhou, and Ma Quanjie to Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Huangfu Yu, military governor of Huazhou, to march on Xingzhou and Ma Quanjie on Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 契丹寇洺、磁，犯鄴都西北界，所在告急。

translations.literal: The Khitan raided Ming and Ci, violated the northwest border of Yedu, and urgent reports came in from every quarter.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan struck Ming and Ci, crossed into Yedu's northwestern marches, and alarms poured in from every side.

sentences.zh: 壬子，王師與契丹相拒於相州北安陽河上，皇甫遇、慕容彥超率前鋒與敵騎戰於榆林店，遇馬中流矢，僅而獲免。

translations.literal: On renzi, the imperial army and the Khitan faced one another north of the Anyang River at Xiangzhou; Huangfu Yu and Murong Yanchao led the vanguard against the enemy cavalry at Yulin Post; Yu's horse was struck by a flying arrow, and he barely escaped.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi, the imperial army and the Khitan confronted each other north of the Anyang River at Xiangzhou. Huangfu Yu and Murong Yanchao led the vanguard against enemy cavalry at Yulin Post; Yu's horse took a stray arrow and he barely got away.

sentences.zh: 〈（《遼史》：皇甫遇與濮州刺史慕容彥超將兵千騎，來覘遼軍。

translations.literal: (From the 《History of Liao》: Huangfu Yu and Murong Yanchao, prefect of Pu Prefecture, led a thousand horsemen to reconnoiter the Liao army.
translations.idiomatic: (From the 《History of Liao》: Huangfu Yu and Murong Yanchao, prefect of Pu, led a thousand cavalry to scout the Liao forces.

sentences.zh: 至鄴都，遇遼軍數萬，且戰且卻，至榆林店，遼軍繼至，遇與彥超力戰百餘合，遇馬斃步戰，安審琦引騎兵逾水以救，遼軍乃還。）〉

translations.literal: At Yedu they met tens of thousands of Liao troops, fighting while retreating; at Yulin Post the Liao army came up in succession; Yu and Yanchao fought strenuously for more than a hundred engagements; when Yu's horse was killed he fought on foot; An Shenqi led cavalry across the water to rescue them, and the Liao army then withdrew.)〉
translations.idiomatic: At Yedu they encountered tens of thousands of Liao troops and fought their way back. At Yulin Post fresh Liao forces closed in; Yu and Yanchao battled fiercely for more than a hundred bouts. When Yu's horse fell he continued on foot until An Shenqi led cavalry across the river to their aid, and the Liao army withdrew.)〉

sentences.zh: 是夜，張從恩引軍退保黎陽，唯留五百人守安陽河橋。

translations.literal: That night, Zhang Cong'en led his army in retreat to hold Liyang, leaving only five hundred men to guard the Anyang River bridge.
translations.idiomatic: That night Zhang Cong'en pulled back to Liyang, leaving only five hundred men to hold the Anyang River bridge.

sentences.zh: 既而知州符彥倫與軍校謀曰：「此夜紛紜，人無固誌，五百疲兵，安能守橋！」

translations.literal: Then the prefect Fu Yanlun and the army officers plotted together, saying, "Tonight is chaos—men have no fixed resolve; five hundred weary soldiers—how can they hold the bridge!"
translations.idiomatic: Then Prefect Fu Yanlun and his officers conferred: "Tonight everything is in turmoil and no man's mind is settled. Five hundred exhausted soldiers cannot hold this bridge!"

sentences.zh: 即抽入相州，嬰城為備。

translations.literal: They thereupon withdrew into Xiangzhou and closed the city to prepare defenses.
translations.idiomatic: They withdrew at once into Xiangzhou, shut the gates, and made ready to defend the city.

sentences.zh: 至曙，賊軍萬餘騎已陣於安陽河北，彥倫令城上揚旗鼓噪，賊不之測。

translations.literal: At dawn, more than ten thousand enemy horsemen had already drawn up north of the Anyang River; Yanlun ordered drums and banners raised on the walls with a great clamor, and the enemy could not fathom their strength.
translations.idiomatic: At daybreak more than ten thousand enemy horsemen were already formed north of the Anyang River. Yanlun had drums beaten and banners raised on the walls with a great shout, and the enemy could not gauge his strength.

sentences.zh: 至辰時，渡河而南，悉陣甲騎於城下，如攻城之狀。

translations.literal: By the hour of chen they forded the river and went south, arraying all armored cavalry below the city as if to assault it.
translations.idiomatic: By the hour of chen they crossed the river and marched south, drawing up every armored horseman below the walls as though preparing to storm the city.

sentences.zh: 彥倫曰：「此敵將走矣。」

translations.literal: Yanlun said, "The enemy is about to withdraw."
translations.idiomatic: Yanlun said, "These enemies are about to pull away."

sentences.zh: 乃出甲士五百於城北，張弓弩以待之，契丹果引去。

translations.literal: He then sent out five hundred armored soldiers north of the city, strung bows and crossbows, and waited; the Khitan indeed withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: He sent five hundred armored men out through the north gate with bows and crossbows at the ready; the Khitan, as he had foreseen, withdrew.

sentences.zh: 當皇甫遇榆林戰時，至晚敵眾自相驚曰：「晉軍悉至矣。」

translations.literal: During Huangfu Yu's battle at Yulin Post, by evening the enemy masses alarmed one another, saying, "The Jin armies have all arrived!"
translations.idiomatic: While Huangfu Yu was fighting at Yulin Post, by evening the enemy ranks panicked one another, crying, "All the Jin armies have come!"

sentences.zh: 戎王在邯鄲聞之，即時北遁，官軍亦南保黎陽。

translations.literal: The Khitan ruler, at Handan, heard this and fled north at once; the imperial army also withdrew south to hold Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan ruler, then at Handan, heard it and fled north at once; the imperial army likewise fell back south to Liyang.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，以河陽留後李建崇為邢州留後，以鳳州防禦使

translations.literal: On jiayin, Li Jianchong, regent of Heyang, was made regent of Xingzhou, and Fang Tai, defense commissioner of Fengzhou
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin, Li Jianchong, regent of Heyang, was appointed regent of Xingzhou, and Fang Tai, defense commissioner of Fengzhou

sentences.zh: 〈（案：此下有闕文。）〉

translations.literal: (Editor's note: text is missing below in the source.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (Note: the original text is missing at this point.)〉

sentences.zh: 為河陽留後。

translations.literal: He was made regent of Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed regent of Heyang.

sentences.zh: 詔李守貞領兵屯滑州，以宣徽北院使李彥韜權侍衛馬步都虞候。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Li Shouzhen to lead troops and encamp at Huazhou, and Li Yantao, Commissioner of the North Court of the Palace Secretariat, was made acting overall deputy commander of the palace horse and foot armies.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Li Shouzhen to encamp at Huazhou, and Li Yantao, commissioner of the North Court of the Palace Secretariat, was made acting overall deputy commander of the palace horse and foot armies.

sentences.zh: 改諸道武定軍為天威軍。

translations.literal: The Martial Stability Armies of the various circuits were renamed the Heavenly Majesty Army.
translations.idiomatic: The Martial Stability Armies of every circuit were redesignated the Heavenly Majesty Army.

sentences.zh: 己未，以前許州節度使李從溫為北面行營都招撫使，以鄆州節度使張從恩權東京留守。

translations.literal: On jiwei, Li Congwen, former military governor of Xuzhou, was made overall commander for pacification of the Northern Campaign Headquarters; Zhang Cong'en, military governor of Yanzhou, was made acting regent of the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei, Li Congwen, former military governor of Xuzhou, was made overall pacification commander of the northern campaign; Zhang Cong'en, military governor of Yanzhou, was appointed acting regent of the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，相州奏，契丹抽退，其鄉村避寇百姓，已發遣各歸本家營種。

translations.literal: On xinyou, Xiangzhou memorialized that the Khitan had withdrawn, and the common people of the countryside who had fled the raiders had been sent back to their homes to resume farming.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou, Xiangzhou reported that the Khitan had pulled back and that villagers who had fled the raids had been sent home to resume their planting.

sentences.zh: 初，帝以不豫初平，未任親禦軍旅，既而張從恩、馬全節相次奏賊軍充斥，恒州杜威告事勢危急，帝曰：「北敵未平，固難安寢，當悉眾一戰，以救朔方生靈。

translations.literal: Earlier, because the Emperor's illness had only just eased, he was not yet able to command the armies in person; then Zhang Cong'en and Ma Quanjie in succession memorialized that enemy armies filled the land, and Du Wei of Hengzhou reported that the situation was critically urgent. The Emperor said, "The northern enemy is not yet subdued—how can I rest in peace? We must muster all our forces for one decisive battle to save the people of the northern frontier.
translations.idiomatic: At first, with his illness only just abating, the Emperor was not yet fit to take personal command; then Zhang Cong'en and Ma Quanjie reported in turn that enemy armies swarmed everywhere, and Du Wei at Hengzhou warned that the crisis was acute. The Emperor said, "The northern foe is still abroad—how can I sleep easy? We must throw every man into one great battle to rescue the people of the north.

sentences.zh: 若宴安遲疑，則大河以北，淪為寇壤矣。」

translations.literal: If we feast in ease and hesitate, then north of the Great River all will become enemy territory."
translations.idiomatic: If we linger in comfort and doubt, everything north of the Yellow River will fall to the invaders."

sentences.zh: 即日命諸將點閱，以定行計。

translations.literal: That same day he ordered the generals to muster and review the troops to fix the plan of march.
translations.idiomatic: That same day he ordered the generals to muster and inspect the troops and settle the plan of campaign.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，下詔親征。

translations.literal: On xinyou, an edict was issued for a personal campaign.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou, an edict proclaimed the Emperor's personal expedition.

sentences.zh: 誅楊光遠部下指揮使張迥等五人，以戎事方興，慮其扇搖故也。

translations.literal: Zhang Jiong and four other commanders under Yang Guangyuan were executed—because military affairs were just rising, and there was fear they might stir unrest.
translations.idiomatic: Five commanders who had served under Yang Guangyuan, including Zhang Jiong, were put to death—for war was at hand, and the court feared they might incite mutiny.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，以樞密直學士李穀為三司副使，判留司三司公事。

translations.literal: On guihai, Li Gu, Direct Academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs, was made Deputy Commissioner of the Three Commissions and was assigned to manage the affairs of the Three Commissions left behind at the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai, Li Gu, Direct Academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs, was made deputy commissioner of the Three Commissions with charge of capital-side Three Commissions business.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，車駕發離京師。

translations.literal: On yichou, the imperial carriage set out from the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou, the imperial procession left the capital.

sentences.zh: 是月，京城北壕春冰之上有文，若大樹花葉，凡數十株，宛若圖畫，觀者如堵。

translations.literal: That month, on the spring ice atop the northern moat of the capital there appeared markings like great trees with flowers and leaves—several tens of them in all, as if painted; viewers packed the streets.
translations.idiomatic: That month, patterns like flowering trees appeared on the spring ice above the capital's northern moat—several dozen in all, as vivid as paintings—and crowds of onlookers filled the streets.

sentences.zh: 二月戊辰朔，車駕次滑州。

translations.literal: On the first day of the second month, wuchen, the imperial carriage halted at Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: On the new moon of the second month, wuchen, the imperial train stopped at Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 己巳，渡浮橋，幸黎陽勞軍，至晚還滑州。

translations.literal: On jisi, he crossed the pontoon bridge, visited Liyang to review the troops, and returned to Huazhou in the evening.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi he crossed the floating bridge, went to Liyang to review the troops, and returned to Huazhou that evening.

sentences.zh: 以滄州節度使田武充東北面行營都部署。

translations.literal: Tian Wu, military governor of Cangzhou, was appointed overall deployment commander of the northeastern campaign headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Wu, military governor of Cangzhou, was made overall deployment commander of the northeastern campaign.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，幸澶州，以景延廣為隨駕馬步軍都鈐轄。

translations.literal: On jiaxu, he visited Chazhou and made Jing Yanguang overall controller of the horse and foot armies accompanying the imperial progress.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu he proceeded to Chazhou and appointed Jing Yanguang overall controller of the escort horse and foot armies.

sentences.zh: 丙子，大閱諸軍於戚城，帝親臨之。

translations.literal: On bingzi, a great review of the armies was held at Qicheng, and the Emperor attended in person.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi the armies were reviewed in grand array at Qicheng, with the Emperor presiding in person.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，北面行營副招討使馬全節、行營都監李守貞、右神武統軍張彥澤等以前軍先發。

translations.literal: On wuyin, Ma Quanjie, deputy commander for suppression of the Northern Campaign Headquarters, Li Shouzhen, overall supervisor of the field headquarters, Zhang Yanzhe, Right Commander of the Spirit Martial Army, and others led the advance guard out first.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin, Ma Quanjie, deputy pacification commander of the northern campaign, Li Shouzhen, overall supervisor of the field headquarters, Zhang Yanzhe, Right Commander of the Spirit Martial Army, and others marched out with the vanguard.

sentences.zh: 己卯，以許州節度使符彥卿為北面行營馬軍都指揮使，以左神武統軍潘環為北面行營步軍都指揮使。

translations.literal: On jimao, Fu Yanqing, military governor of Xuzhou, was made overall commander of the cavalry of the Northern Campaign Headquarters; Pan Huan, Left Commander of the Spirit Martial Army, was made overall commander of the infantry of the Northern Campaign Headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao, Fu Yanqing, military governor of Xuzhou, was made overall cavalry commander of the northern campaign, and Pan Huan, Left Commander of the Spirit Martial Army, overall infantry commander.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，幸楊村故壘。

translations.literal: On xinsi, he visited the old fort at Yang Village.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi he inspected the old fort at Yang Village.

sentences.zh: 符彥卿、皇甫遇、李殷率諸軍進發。

translations.literal: Fu Yanqing, Huangfu Yu, and Li Yin led the various armies forward.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Yanqing, Huangfu Yu, and Li Yin advanced with the combined armies.

sentences.zh: 以左散騎常侍邊光範為樞密直學士。

translations.literal: Bian Guangfan, Left Regular Attendant of the Cavalry, was made Direct Academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Bian Guangfan, Left Regular Attendant of the Cavalry, was appointed Direct Academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 詔河北諸州，應蕃騎經由之地，吏民遭殺害者，委所在收瘞，量事祭奠。

translations.literal: An edict to the prefectures of Hebei ordered that wherever Khitan cavalry had passed, officials and commoners who had been killed were to be collected and buried by the local authorities, with rites of mourning performed as circumstances allowed.
translations.idiomatic: An edict to the Hebei prefectures directed that wherever Khitan horsemen had passed, local authorities were to gather and bury officials and commoners who had been slain and perform such mourning rites as the case allowed.

sentences.zh: 詔恒州杜威與馬全節等會合進軍。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Du Wei of Hengzhou to join Ma Quanjie and the others in advancing.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Du Wei at Hengzhou to unite with Ma Quanjie and the others and advance.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，幸鐵丘閱馬，因幸趙在禮、李從溫軍。

translations.literal: On bingxu, he reviewed horses at Tieqiu and then visited the armies of Zhao Zaili and Li Congwen.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu he reviewed horses at Iron Mound, then inspected the camps of Zhao Zaili and Li Congwen.

sentences.zh: 是日大雪。

translations.literal: That day, heavy snow fell.
translations.idiomatic: That day brought heavy snow.

sentences.zh: 戊子，安審琦、梁漢璋領兵北征。

translations.literal: On wuzi, An Shenqi and Liang Hanzhang led troops on the northern expedition.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi, An Shenqi and Liang Hanzhang marched north on campaign.

sentences.zh: 府州防禦使折從阮奏，部領兵士攻圍契丹勝州，降之，見進兵趨朔州。

translations.literal: Zhe Congruan, defense commissioner of Fuzhou, memorialized that he had led his soldiers to besiege and attack the Khitan at Shengzhou, reduced it, and saw the advancing army pressing toward Shuozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhe Congruan, defense commissioner of Fuzhou, reported that he had besieged the Khitan at Shengzhou, taken it, and saw the advancing army pressing toward Shuozhou.

sentences.zh: 甲午，以河中節度使安審琦為北面行營馬步軍都虞候，許州節度使符彥卿充馬步軍左廂都指揮使，滑州節度使皇甫遇充馬步軍右廂都指揮使，侍衛馬軍都指揮使梁漢璋充馬軍左右廂都指揮使，侍衛步軍都指揮使李殷充步軍左右廂都指揮使，左神武統軍張彥澤充馬軍左右廂都排陣使，右神武統軍潘環充步軍左右廂排陣使。

translations.literal: On jiawu, An Shenqi, military governor of Hezhong, was made overall deputy commander of the horse and foot armies of the Northern Campaign Headquarters; Fu Yanqing, military governor of Xuzhou, was appointed overall commander of the left wing of the horse and foot armies; Huangfu Yu, military governor of Huazhou, was appointed overall commander of the right wing of the horse and foot armies; Liang Hanzhang, Commander of the Palace Cavalry, was appointed overall commander of both wings of the cavalry; Li Yin, Commander of the Palace Infantry, was appointed overall commander of both wings of the infantry; Zhang Yanzhe, Left Commander of the Spirit Martial Army, was appointed overall array marshal of both wings of the cavalry; Pan Huan, Right Commander of the Spirit Martial Army, was appointed array marshal of both wings of the infantry.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu, An Shenqi, military governor of Hezhong, became overall deputy commander of the northern campaign horse and foot; Fu Yanqing of Xuzhou, overall commander of the left wing; Huangfu Yu of Huazhou, overall commander of the right wing; Palace Cavalry Commander Liang Hanzhang, overall commander of both cavalry wings; Palace Infantry Commander Li Yin, overall commander of both infantry wings; Left Spirit Martial Commander Zhang Yanzhe, overall array marshal of both cavalry wings; and Right Spirit Martial Commander Pan Huan, array marshal of both infantry wings.

sentences.zh: 丙申，以端明殿學士、尚書戶部侍郎馮玉為戶部尚書，充樞密使。

translations.literal: On bingshen, Feng Yu, Direct Academician of the Duanming Hall and Vice Minister of Revenue, was made Minister of Revenue and appointed Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen, Feng Yu, Direct Academician of the Duanming Hall and Vice Minister of Revenue, was promoted to Minister of Revenue and appointed military affairs commissioner.

sentences.zh: 三月戊戌，契丹陷祁州，刺史沈斌死之。

translations.literal: On the third month, wuxu, the Khitan captured Qizhou; Prefect Shen Bin died in the defense.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on wuxu, the Khitan took Qizhou; Prefect Shen Bin died defending it.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，左補闕袁範先陷契丹，自賊中逃歸。

translations.literal: On yisi, Left Remonstrance Official Yuan Fanxian, who had earlier fallen to the Khitan, escaped from the enemy and returned.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi, Left Remonstrance Official Yuan Fanxian, who had earlier been taken by the Khitan, fled from the enemy camp and returned.

sentences.zh: 杜威奏，與李守貞、馬全節、安審琦、皇甫遇部領大軍赴定州。

translations.literal: Du Wei memorialized that he, together with Li Shouzhen, Ma Quanjie, An Shenqi, and Huangfu Yu, were leading the great army toward Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Du Wei reported that he was marching the main army toward Dingzhou with Li Shouzhen, Ma Quanjie, An Shenqi, and Huangfu Yu.

sentences.zh: 易州刺史安審約奏，二月三日夜，差壯丁斫敵營，殺敵十餘人。

translations.literal: An Shenyao, prefect of Yizhou, memorialized that on the third night of the second month he had sent strong men to cut into the enemy camp and killed more than ten of the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: An Shenyao, prefect of Yizhou, reported that on the third night of the second month he had sent stout men to raid the enemy camp and killed more than ten men.

sentences.zh: 是日，以符彥卿為北面行營馬步軍左右廂都排陣使，以皇甫遇為北面行營馬步軍左廂排陣使，以王周為馬步軍右廂排陣使。

translations.literal: That day, Fu Yanqing was made overall array marshal of both wings of the horse and foot armies of the Northern Campaign Headquarters; Huangfu Yu was made left-wing array marshal of the horse and foot armies of the Northern Campaign Headquarters; Wang Zhou was made right-wing array marshal of the horse and foot armies.
translations.idiomatic: That day, Fu Yanqing was made overall array marshal of both horse-and-foot wings of the northern campaign; Huangfu Yu, left-wing array marshal; and Wang Zhou, right-wing array marshal.

sentences.zh: 丁未，畋於戚城，還幸景延廣、安審信軍。

translations.literal: On dingwei, he hunted at Qicheng, then visited the armies of Jing Yanguang and An Shenxin.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei he hunted at Qicheng, then inspected the camps of Jing Yanguang and An Shenxin.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，王師攻泰州，刺史晉庭謙以城降。

translations.literal: On gengxu, the imperial army attacked Taizhou; Prefect Jin Tingqian surrendered the city.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu the imperial army attacked Taizhou, and Prefect Jin Tingqian surrendered the city.

sentences.zh: 易州奏，郎山塞將孫方簡破契丹千餘人，斬蕃將諧裏相公，擄其妻以獻。

translations.literal: Yizhou memorialized that Sun Fangjian, garrison commander of Langshan Pass, had broken more than a thousand Khitan, beheaded the Khitan general Xieli Xianggong, and presented his captive wife.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhou reported that Sun Fangjian, garrison commander at Langshan Pass, had routed more than a thousand Khitan, beheaded the Khitan general Xieli Xianggong, and sent his captured wife as tribute.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，杜威奏，收復滿城，獲契丹首領沒剌相公，並蕃漢兵士二千人。

translations.literal: On jiayin, Du Wei memorialized that Mancheng had been recovered and that the Khitan leader Molie Xianggong had been captured, together with two thousand Khitan and Han soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin, Du Wei reported the recovery of Mancheng and the capture of the Khitan leader Molie Xianggong along with two thousand Khitan and Han troops.

sentences.zh: 以前戶部尚書李懌為兵部尚書。

translations.literal: Li Yun, former Minister of Revenue, was made Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yun, former Minister of Revenue, was appointed Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，杜威奏，收復遂城。

translations.literal: On yimao, Du Wei memorialized that Suicheng had been recovered.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao, Du Wei reported the recovery of Suicheng.

sentences.zh: 丙辰奏，大軍自遂城卻退至滿城。

translations.literal: On bingchen it was memorialized that the great army had withdrawn from Suicheng back to Mancheng.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen came word that the main army had pulled back from Suicheng to Mancheng.

sentences.zh: 時賊將趙延壽部曲來降，言：「契丹主昨至古北口，幽州走報，漢軍大下，收卻泰州。

translations.literal: At that time followers of the enemy general Zhao Yanshou came over in surrender, saying, "Yesterday the Khitan ruler reached Gubeikou; couriers fled from Youzhou with word that the Han armies were descending in force and had retaken Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Just then men from the command of the enemy general Zhao Yanshou defected, reporting, "Yesterday the Khitan ruler reached Gubeikou; fugitives from Youzhou brought word that Han armies were marching down in strength and had retaken Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 尋下令諸部，令輜重入塞，輕騎卻回。

translations.literal: Soon orders went out to the various divisions to send baggage trains back inside the passes and have the light cavalry withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered every division to send its baggage back through the passes and pull the light cavalry away.

sentences.zh: 戎王率五萬餘騎，來勢極盛，明日前鋒必至，請為之備。」

translations.literal: The Khitan ruler is leading more than fifty thousand horsemen; his momentum is extremely strong; the vanguard will surely arrive tomorrow—please prepare against them."
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan ruler is coming south at the head of more than fifty thousand horsemen in overwhelming force; his vanguard will reach us tomorrow—make ready at once."

sentences.zh: 杜威、李守貞謀曰：「我師糧運不繼，深入賊疆，而逢大敵，亡之道也。

translations.literal: Du Wei and Li Shouzhen plotted together, saying, "Our army's grain supply cannot keep up; we have penetrated deep into enemy territory and now meet a great foe—this is the road to destruction.
translations.idiomatic: Du Wei and Li Shouzhen conferred: "Our grain cannot keep pace; we are deep in enemy country and now face a massive foe—this is the path to annihilation.

sentences.zh: 不如退還泰州，觀其兵勢強弱而禦之。」

translations.literal: Better to withdraw to Taizhou, observe the enemy's strength or weakness, and then resist them."
translations.idiomatic: Better to fall back to Taizhou, watch the enemy's strength, and meet them from there."

sentences.zh: 軍士皆以為然。

translations.literal: The soldiers all agreed that this was right.
translations.idiomatic: The troops all agreed.

sentences.zh: 是日，還滿城。

translations.literal: That day, they returned to Mancheng.
translations.idiomatic: That day they fell back to Mancheng.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，至泰州。

translations.literal: On dingsi, they reached Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi they reached Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 戊午，契丹前鋒已至。

translations.literal: On wuwu, the Khitan vanguard had already arrived.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu the Khitan vanguard was already on the field.

sentences.zh: 己未，大軍發泰州而南，契丹踵其後。

translations.literal: On jiwei, the great army set out from Taizhou and marched south; the Khitan followed on their heels.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei the main army marched south from Taizhou with the Khitan treading on its heels.

sentences.zh: 是日，次陽城。

translations.literal: That day, they halted at Yangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: That day they encamped at Yangcheng.

sentences.zh: 庚申，敵騎如墻而來，我步軍為方陣以禦之。

translations.literal: On gengshen, enemy cavalry came on like a wall; our infantry formed a square battle formation to meet them.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen enemy cavalry closed in like a moving rampart; our infantry drew up in square formation to receive them.

sentences.zh: 選勁騎擊賊，鬥二十餘合，南行十餘里，賊勢稍卻，渡白溝而去。

translations.literal: Picked cavalry were chosen to strike the enemy; they fought more than twenty engagements, marched south more than ten li, the enemy's momentum gradually slackened, and they crossed the Bai Gou and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Elite cavalry were sent to hit the enemy; after more than twenty clashes and a march of more than ten li southward, the enemy's pressure eased and they crossed the White Ditch and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，杜威召諸將議曰：「戎首自來，實為敵，若不血戰，吾輩何以求免。」

translations.literal: On xinyou, Du Wei summoned the generals to counsel, saying, "The barbarian chief has come in person—he is truly the enemy; if we do not fight to the death, how shall any of us hope to escape?"
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou, Du Wei called the generals together and said, "The Khitan ruler has come in person—this is the enemy himself. Unless we fight to the blood, none of us will get out alive."

sentences.zh: 諸將然之。

translations.literal: The generals agreed.
translations.idiomatic: The generals assented.

sentences.zh: 是日，敵騎還繞官軍，相去數里。

translations.literal: That day, enemy cavalry circled back around the imperial army, several li apart.
translations.idiomatic: That day enemy cavalry wheeled around the imperial army, keeping several li away.

sentences.zh: 明日，我軍成列而行，蕃漢轉鬥，殺聲震地，才行十餘里，軍中人馬饑乏。

translations.literal: The next day, our army marched in battle order; Khitan and Han fought in turn, and the cries of killing shook the earth; they had gone only a little more than ten li when men and horses within the army were hungry and exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: The next day our army marched in formed ranks; Khitan and Han traded blows until the battle cries shook the ground; after barely more than ten li, men and horses were starving and spent.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，大軍至白團衛村下營。

translations.literal: On guihai, the great army encamped below Baituanwei Village.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai the main army made camp below Baituanwei Village.

sentences.zh: 人馬俱渴，營中掘井，及水輒壞，兵士取其泥絞汁而飲。

translations.literal: Men and horses alike were parched; in camp they dug wells, but as soon as water was reached the earth collapsed; soldiers took the mud and wrung out the juice to drink.
translations.idiomatic: Men and horses were alike parched with thirst; within the camp they dug wells, but the moment water appeared the sides caved in; soldiers squeezed mud and drank the drippings.

sentences.zh: 敵眾圍繞，漸束其營。

translations.literal: The enemy masses surrounded them and gradually tightened the ring around the camp.
translations.idiomatic: Enemy forces ringed them in and slowly drew the noose tighter around the camp.

sentences.zh: 〈（《宋史·藥元福傳》：晉師列方陣，設拒馬為行寨，契丹以奇兵出陣後，斷糧道。）〉

translations.literal: (From the 《Song History · Biography of Yao Yuanfu》: The Jin army formed a square battle formation and set up caltrop barriers as a marching camp; the Khitan sent a surprise force out behind the battle line and cut the supply route.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (From the 《Song History · Biography of Yao Yuanfu》: The Jin army drew up in square formation and erected caltrop palisades for a marching encampment; the Khitan sent flanking troops around behind the formation and severed the grain road.)〉

sentences.zh: 是日，東北風猛，揚塵折樹。

translations.literal: That day, a fierce northeast wind blew, raising dust and snapping trees.
translations.idiomatic: That day a violent northeast wind rose, whipping up dust and breaking trees.

sentences.zh: 契丹主坐車中謂眾曰：「漢軍盡來，只有此耳，今日並可生擒，然後平定天下。」

translations.literal: The Khitan ruler, sitting in his carriage, said to the multitude, "All the Han armies have come—there are only these; today we can capture them alive, and then pacify the realm."
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan ruler, seated in his carriage, told his host, "Every Han army is here—this is all there is. Today we can take them alive, and then the realm will be ours."

sentences.zh: 令下馬拔鹿角，飛矢雨集。

translations.literal: He ordered them to dismount and pull up the antler stakes; flying arrows fell like rain.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered his men to dismount and tear up the antler palisades; arrows fell like rain.

sentences.zh: 軍士大呼曰：「招討使何不用軍，而令士卒虛死！」

translations.literal: The soldiers shouted loudly, "Commander for suppression, why do you not use the army, yet let the troops die in vain!"
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers roared, "Commander for suppression, why will you not commit the army and instead leave the men to die for nothing!"

sentences.zh: 諸將鹹請擊之。

translations.literal: All the generals together requested permission to attack.
translations.idiomatic: The generals all urged an attack.

sentences.zh: 杜威曰：「俟風勢稍慢，觀其進退。」

translations.literal: Du Wei said, "Wait until the wind slackens somewhat and observe whether they advance or withdraw."
translations.idiomatic: Du Wei said, "Wait until the wind eases and see whether they advance or retreat."

sentences.zh: 守貞曰：「此風助我也。

translations.literal: Shouzhen said, "This wind is helping us.
translations.idiomatic: Shouzhen said, "This wind is on our side.

sentences.zh: 彼眾我寡，黑風之內，莫測多少，若候風止，我輩無噍類矣。」
