translations.literal: They are many and we are few; within this black wind no one can tell their numbers. If we wait for the wind to stop, not one of us will be left alive."
translations.idiomatic: They outnumber us, and in this pitch-dark wind no one can tell how many they are. If we wait for the wind to die, none of us will survive."

sentences.zh: 即呼眾軍齊力擊賊。

translations.literal: He thereupon called on the whole army to strike the enemy with united force.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered the whole army to attack the enemy together.

sentences.zh: 張彥澤、符彥卿、皇甫遇等率騎奮擊，風勢尤猛，沙塵如夜，敵遂大敗。

translations.literal: Zhang Yanzhe, Fu Yanqing, Huangfu Yu, and others led the cavalry in fierce attack; the wind grew still fiercer and sand and dust were like night, and the enemy was utterly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yanzhe, Fu Yanqing, Huangfu Yu, and others led the cavalry in a furious charge; the wind howled harder still and sand blotted out the sky like night, and the enemy was routed.

sentences.zh: 〈（《宋史·符彥卿傳》：時晉師居下風，將戰，弓弩莫施。

translations.literal: (From the 《Song History》 · Biography of Fu Yanqing: At that time the Jin army was downwind; as battle was about to begin, bows and crossbows could not be used.
translations.idiomatic: (From the 《Song History》 · Biography of Fu Yanqing: The Jin army was downwind, and as battle was joined their bows and crossbows were useless.

sentences.zh: 彥卿謂張彥澤、皇甫遇曰：「與其束手就擒，曷若死戰，然未必死。」

translations.literal: Yanqing said to Zhang Yanzhe and Huangfu Yu, "Rather than wait helplessly to be captured, how much better to fight to the death—yet we may not die after all."
translations.idiomatic: Yanqing told Zhang Yanzhe and Huangfu Yu, "Better to fight to the death than be taken alive—and we may not die at all."

sentences.zh: 彥澤然之，遂潛兵尾其後，順風擊之，契丹大敗。

translations.literal: Yanzhe agreed; thereupon they secretly sent troops to follow behind the enemy and struck with the wind at their backs, and the Khitan were utterly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhe agreed; they sent troops quietly around the enemy's rear and struck with the wind at their backs, routing the Khitan.

sentences.zh: 又，《藥元福傳》：守貞與元福謀曰：「軍中饑渴已甚，若候風反出戰，吾屬為虜矣。

translations.literal: Moreover, from the 《Song History》 · Biography of Yao Yuanfu: Shouzhen and Yuanfu plotted together, saying, "The army is already desperately hungry and thirsty; if we wait for the wind to turn before fighting, we shall all become captives.
translations.idiomatic: Also, from the 《Song History》 · Biography of Yao Yuanfu: Shouzhen and Yuanfu conferred: "The troops are starving and parched; if we wait for the wind to shift before fighting, we are finished.

sentences.zh: 彼謂我不能逆風以戰，宜出其不意以擊之，此兵家之奇也。」

translations.literal: They think we cannot fight against the wind; we should take them unawares and strike—this is a classic stratagem of war."
translations.idiomatic: They assume we cannot fight into the wind; we should surprise them—classic military audacity."

sentences.zh: 元福乃率麾下開拒馬出戰，諸將繼至，契丹大敗。）〉

translations.literal: Yuanfu then led his men to open the abatis and go out to battle; the other generals followed, and the Khitan were utterly defeated.)〉
translations.idiomatic: Yuanfu led his men out through the abatis; the other generals joined in, and the Khitan were routed.)〉

sentences.zh: 時步騎齊進，追襲二十餘里。

translations.literal: At that time infantry and cavalry advanced together in pursuit for more than twenty li.
translations.idiomatic: Infantry and cavalry pressed the pursuit together for more than twenty li.

sentences.zh: 至陽城東，賊軍稍稍成列，我騎復擊之，乃渡河而去。

translations.literal: East of Yangcheng the enemy troops gradually formed ranks; our cavalry struck them again, and they thereupon crossed the river and departed.
translations.idiomatic: East of Yangcheng the enemy began to form ranks; our cavalry struck again, and they crossed the river and fled.

sentences.zh: 守貞曰：「今日危急極矣，幸諸君奮命，吾事獲濟。

translations.literal: Shouzhen said, "Today was the utmost extremity of peril; thanks to you all fighting with your lives, our cause has been saved.
translations.idiomatic: Shouzhen said, "Today we reached the brink of ruin; thanks to your desperate fighting, we have been saved.

sentences.zh: 兩日以來，人馬渴乏，今吃水之後，腳重難行，速宜收軍定州，保全而還，上策也。」

translations.literal: For two days men and horses have been parched and exhausted; now that they have drunk their fill, their legs are heavy and hard to move. We should quickly withdraw the army to Dingzhou and return intact—that is the best plan."
translations.idiomatic: For two days men and horses have gone without water; now that they have drunk their fill they are sluggish. We should withdraw quickly to Dingzhou and return intact—that is the wisest course."

sentences.zh: 由是諸將整眾而還。

translations.literal: Thereupon the generals reformed their troops and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The generals thereupon reformed their columns and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 是時，契丹主坐車中，及敗走，車行十餘里，追兵既急，獲一橐駝，乘之而走。

translations.literal: At that time the Khitan ruler was seated in his carriage; when he was defeated and fled, the carriage went more than ten li, but as the pursuing troops pressed close he obtained a Bactrian camel, mounted it, and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan ruler had been riding in his carriage; when he fled in defeat the carriage covered more than ten li, but as pursuit closed in he seized a Bactrian camel, mounted it, and escaped.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，杜威等大軍自定州班師入恒州。

translations.literal: On yichou, Du Wei and the other commanders led the great army back from Dingzhou in formal withdrawal and entered Hengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou, Du Wei and the main army withdrew from Dingzhou and entered Hengzhou.

sentences.zh: 夏四月丙子，以車駕將還京，差官往西京告天地宗廟社稷。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on bingzi, because the imperial carriage was about to return to the capital, officials were dispatched to the Western Capital to announce the fact to Heaven and Earth, the ancestral temples, and the altars of soil and grain.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer, on bingzi, as the Emperor was about to return to the capital, envoys were sent to the Western Capital to report to Heaven and Earth, the ancestral temples, and the altars of state.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，駕發澶州。

translations.literal: On xinsi, the imperial carriage departed from Chanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi, the imperial procession left Chanzhou.

sentences.zh: 甲申，至京師，曲赦在京禁囚。

translations.literal: On jiashen, the court arrived at the capital and granted a partial amnesty to prisoners held in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen, the court reached the capital and granted a partial amnesty to prisoners in the capital.

sentences.zh: 己亥，詔鄴都依舊為天雄軍。

translations.literal: On jihai, an edict declared that Yedu was again to be the Tianxiong Army.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai, an edict restored Yedu as headquarters of the Tianxiong Army.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，河東節度使劉知遠封北平王；

translations.literal: On gengyin, Liu Zhiyuan, military governor of Hedong, was enfeoffed as Prince of Beiping;
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin, Liu Zhiyuan, military governor of Hedong, was enfeoffed as Prince of Beiping;

sentences.zh: 恒州節度使杜威加守太傅；

translations.literal: Du Wei, military governor of Hengzhou, was given the additional title of Acting Grand Tutor;
translations.idiomatic: Du Wei of Hengzhou received the honorary title of Acting Grand Tutor;

sentences.zh: 徐州趙在禮移鎮兗州；

translations.literal: Zhao Zaili of Xuzhou was transferred to Yanzhou;
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Zaili of Xuzhou was transferred to Yanzhou;

sentences.zh: 宋州節度使兼侍衛親軍馬步都指揮使高行周移鎮鄆州，侍衛如故；

translations.literal: Gao Xingzhou, military governor of Songzhou with concurrent appointment as overall commander of horse and foot of the palace guard, was transferred to Yanzhou, retaining his palace guard duties;
translations.idiomatic: Gao Xingzhou, military governor of Songzhou and overall commander of the palace guard horse and foot, was transferred to Yanzhou while keeping his guard command;

sentences.zh: 鄴都留守馬全節改天雄軍節度使；

translations.literal: Ma Quanjie, military commissioner of Yedu, was made military governor of the Tianxiong Army;
translations.idiomatic: Ma Quanjie, military commissioner of Yedu, became military governor of the Tianxiong Army;

sentences.zh: 兗州節度使兼侍衛都虞候李守貞移鎮宋州，加檢校太師兼侍衛親軍副指揮使；

translations.literal: Li Shouzhen, military governor of Yanzhou with concurrent appointment as overall deputy commander of the palace guard, was transferred to Songzhou, with the additional titles of Grand Preceptor by special appointment and Deputy Overall Commander of the palace guard;
translations.idiomatic: Li Shouzhen of Yanzhou, deputy commander of the palace guard, was transferred to Songzhou and given the honorary title of Grand Preceptor and the post of Deputy Overall Commander of the palace guard;

sentences.zh: 河中節度使安審琦加兼侍中，移鎮許州；

translations.literal: An Shenqi, military governor of Hezhong, was given the additional title of Vice Grand Counselor and transferred to Xuzhou;
translations.idiomatic: An Shenqi of Hezhong was made Vice Grand Counselor and transferred to Xuzhou;

sentences.zh: 許州節度使符彥卿加同平章事，移鎮徐州；

translations.literal: Fu Yanqing, military governor of Xu Prefecture, was given the additional title of Co-Grand Councilor and transferred to Xuzhou;
translations.idiomatic: Fu Yanqing of Xu Prefecture was made Co-Grand Councilor and transferred to Xuzhou;

sentences.zh: 滑州節度使皇甫遇加同平章事。

translations.literal: Huangfu Yu, military governor of Huazhou, was given the additional title of Co-Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: Huangfu Yu of Huazhou was made Co-Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，西京留守景延廣加邑封，改功臣；

translations.literal: On renchen, Jing Yanguang, military commissioner of the Western Capital, was granted an increase in fief and a change of merit-title;
translations.idiomatic: On renchen, Jing Yanguang, military commissioner of the Western Capital, received an enlarged fief and a new merit-title;

sentences.zh: 泰州節度使侯益移鎮河中；

translations.literal: Hou Yi, military governor of Taizhou, was transferred to Hezhong;
translations.idiomatic: Hou Yi of Taizhou was transferred to Hezhong;

sentences.zh: 定州節度使王周加檢校太師。

translations.literal: Wang Zhou, military governor of Dingzhou, was given the additional title of Grand Preceptor by special appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhou of Dingzhou received the honorary title of Grand Preceptor.
